Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0006] Inspect existing modules for error codes and helpers before implementing: Reading models.py, errors.py, money.py, and sibling functions revealed the exact BillingError codes and helpers to reuse.
  Before writing a new function, read the related models, error definitions, and neighboring functions in the same file. Reusing established error codes (invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers (to_money, ZERO) keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.
- [rb-0011] Inspect sibling modules for undocumented team conventions: The first attempt missed idempotency_key, approved_by, and float(amount) audit conventions that were visible in existing modules like payments.py and audit.py.
  Before implementing a new function, read analogous functions in sibling modules (payments.py, audit.py) to infer required keyword-only params, error codes, and audit field formats. These conventions are often not stated in the issue but are enforced by hidden tests.
- [rb-0012] Use money helpers and float for audit amounts: Normalize amounts with to_money/round_money, compare against ZERO, and write float(amount) into audit entries because the ledger JSON importer rejects Decimal.
  Convert inputs via round_money(to_money(amount)), reject non-positive amounts, and accumulate refunded_amount with the same rounding. Always pass float(amount) (and float of running totals) to audit.record to satisfy the ledger service importer.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, wrap raw values with the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of using plain Decimal or float.
  Inspect the money module first and route all arithmetic through its helpers (to_money on inputs, round_money on results, ZERO as the sum seed). This keeps rounding policy consistent and avoids float contamination.
- [rb-0002] Guard division with a zero-total check: For weighted-average or ratio computations, compute the denominator first and return the module's zero constant when it is zero.
  Compute total_quantity (or equivalent denominator) before dividing; if it equals 0, return ZERO rather than dividing. This satisfies the empty-input spec and prevents ZeroDivisionError.
- [rb-0003] Read tests and models before editing: Before writing the implementation, inspect the target test file, models, and money module to learn exact signatures, field names, and expected return types.
  Cat the relevant test and model files in the same step as the source file. This reveals field names (e.g. line.quantity, line.unit_price), expected types, and edge cases, letting the first attempt pass without review feedback.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of raw floats
item.description: When a repo has a money module with to_money/round_money/ZERO, use those for all arithmetic and validation rather than Python floats.
item.content: Read the money helper module before implementing any pricing/amount function. Convert inputs with to_money/round_money, compare against ZERO, and round the final result with round_money to avoid float drift and to match repo conventions.

item.title: Match sibling modules' error conventions
item.description: Before raising errors, grep sibling modules for the project's error class and code style, then mirror it.
item.content: Inspect existing raise sites (e.g. BillingError("non_positive_amount", ...)) to infer the error type and snake_case code pattern. Use the same class and a descriptive code like "invalid_tax_rate" rather than inventing a new exception type.

item.title: Explore repo and tests before writing the implementation
item.description: Start by listing files and reading the target module, related helpers, and existing tests to learn conventions before coding.
item.content: Run a find/ls to map the repo, then cat the target file, its dependency modules (money, errors), and any relevant tests. This surfaces helper APIs and validation patterns, letting the first implementation pass without review feedback.
